paragraphs: Mulberry is a bag maker and fashion company. Its most famous bags include the Bayswater and the Lily. On October 19, news reports shared a sales update from the company. It covered the 26 weeks that ended on September 26, 2026. That is precisely half a year. The update showed considerable growth. Group sales rose 18%, or precisely 18.1%, compared with the same half a year earlier.

Growth varied from market to market. The strongest market was the United States. There, sales grew 28% from a year before. Part of this growth derived from digital sales. The company cited the launch of Bloomingdale's Marketplace, an online store. It also cited more stores in the country that now sell Mulberry bags.

Other overseas markets grew too. In Europe, not counting the United Kingdom, sales rose 23%. Asia Pacific was weaker, with growth of 5%. In the United Kingdom itself, sales grew 10%. So the numbers vary a lot, from 5% to 28%. Two of the three overseas regions grew faster than the United Kingdom.

Mulberry does not only sell in its own stores. Some sales go through franchise partners and other partner stores. In a franchise, another business runs a store with the brand's name. Other partner stores buy goods from the maker and sell them to their own customers. Sales through these partners grew 52%. They made up 17% of all sales, compared with 16% a year earlier.

Buyers stayed keen on the iconic Bayswater and Lily bags. Demand for them was sustained. Additionally, new styles such as the Stevie and the Darley Camera Bag helped. Chief executive Andrea Baldo said the company had worked over the past year to focus again on product, brand and customer.

Most of the growth derived from sales at full price. In other words, buyers paid the normal price, not a lower sale price. Mulberry restricted discounts during the half year. It says it kept discipline in the way it traded. Because it restricted discounts, fewer sales were made at special lower prices. Leaving out some types of price cuts, their share of all sales fell by 3 percentage points. This discipline partly supported the company's margin. The margin is the part of each sale that a company keeps after paying for the goods. According to Baldo, full-price growth demonstrates that buyers in key markets are keen on the collections, even though trading is difficult.

Mulberry also repeated its goals for the medium term. It wants yearly revenue of more than 200 million pounds. It also wants a profit margin of 15%, using the company's own measure. For comparison, revenue in its last full year was 125.5 million pounds. That was up 4% from 120.4 million pounds. So there is still a considerable gap between today's revenue and the goal. The company will share full results for the half year on November 19.
